newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Semis - Spreads hold at tighter levels.
newsitem.headline: Australian Semis - Spreads hold at tighter levels.

text.p: *Semi yield spreads to Australian Treasury debt remained
tight in the wake of last week's announcement by the RBA that
semis will be included in bank's prudential requirements.

Semi-government bond yield spreads to Australian Treasury debt remained tight in the wake of last week's announcement by the Reserve Bank that semi issues will be included in commercial bank's prudential requirements.
The inclusion of semis under bank's prime assets ratios (PAR) had been rumoured for some weeks prior to the RBA's confirmation, which is effective from June 23.

Traders said that the semis market had stabilised at tighter levels, even though there had initially been a feeling that the move had been watered down with the central bank dropping PAR to three percent from six percent.
"Spreads tightened on the PAR announcement and the market has pretty much stabilised at the lows," one trader said.
"Although there has been some natural profit-taking on the move, domestic institutions appear to be short of semis and buyers are around when spreads widen out," he added.
Spreads are now trading around there lowest levels since September last year.

Semi yields have also dropped substantially in the past week as the market outperformed the strong rally in Australian Treasury bonds amid speculation that the RBA will ease monetary policy again following the recent spate of weak data.
Last week's extremely weak labour force data fuelled the speculation and the debt market priced in a 50 basis point easing in current 5.5 percent official interest rates.

However, yields gave up some ground on Tuesday as the market succumbed to a mild correction after 10-year government bond yields dropped to their lowest level in 3-1/4 years and below 7.0 percent on Monday.
